newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir's man wins key Malaysian party post.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir's man wins key Malaysian party post.

text.p: A tearful Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Thursday said corruption and greed will destroy his United Malays National Organisation (UMNO).

"A nation that accepts bribery as its culture may never progress. Corrupt UMNO leaders will sell their souls to whoever offers them more," Mahathir said in an address to UMNO's triennial election assembly, before breaking down in sobs.
Delegates, visibly moved by the prime minister's tears, gave him a standing ovation with shouts of "long live Mahathir".
Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi, a staunch Mahathir ally, was elected one of three vice presidents on Thursday.
Badawi, who has long maintained an image as the "Mr. Clean" of UMNO, lost the post in the last party polls three years ago.
Asked at a news conference if his speech had any bearing on the poll results, Mahathir said: "There may be some effect from my speech this morning but I cannot confirm that."

On Wednesday, Mahathir was dealt a blow when International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz narrowly lost the chairmanship of the women's wing of the party to Deputy Health Minister Siti Zaharah Sulaiman.

Another Mahathir ally, incumbent youth wing chief Rahim Thamby Chik, lost to Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, chairman of a state bank. Both of the winners are seen as aligned to Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
Education Minister Najib Tun Razak and Chief Minister of central Selangor state Muhammad Muhammad Taib retained their vice presidencies in Thursday's polls.
UMNO is the main political party in the ruling National Front coalition, which has governed Malaysia since independence from Britain in 1957.
Mahathir and Anwar were not challenged in the polls, viewed as more significant than a general election, which the National Front has always won easily.

By political convention, the president and deputy president of UMNO serve as prime minister and deputy prime minister. Many of the party contests this week were seen as proxy battles between supporters of the two men.
Badawi lost the vice presidency in 1993 when a team aligned to Anwar swept the top jobs.
Contests for the posts -- which can give the winner access to business opportunities as well -- have become fierce over the past decade due to Malaysia's remarkable economic growth.

One hundred and eighty-five candidates were vying for 66 party positions, including three vice presidencies, 25 seats on the policy-making Supreme Council, and leadership of the youth and women's wings of the party.
Mahathir said a blanket ban on campaigning in the run-up to the elections did not entirely succeed in thwarting "money politics", or vote buying.

"All kinds of restrictions were imposed so that it was alleged no one could move. I said allegedly because the public knows there were campaigns. We know who among the candidates were active, (who) have been using my name and that of the Deputy President (Anwar), and even using money," Mahathir said.
In previous years, campaigning for party posts has seen candidates lavishing money and favours on convention delegates.
On Monday, the party disqualified seven candidates from contesting the elections for trying to buy votes and violating the ban. The UMNO convention finishes on Saturday.
